Belgium battling biggest fire in more than a century as flames near German border and 600 people told to evacuate Two people have died in fires on the Greek island of Salamis as firefighting aircraft were called on to help tame the biggest blaze in Belgium in more than a century in the latest wave of wildfires in Europe. The bodies of two people were recovered from the Peristeria beach area of Salamis on Sunday after two fires broke out on the island, a fire department spokesperson told AFP. Hundreds of people have been ordered to evacuate.

ATHENS, Greece (AP) — Two Greek firefighting helicopters collided in midair on Sunday as they were battling a wind-driven wildfire west of Athens, sending one aircraft crashing to the ground. Two crew members, a Greek and a Danish national, died in the crash. The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe's wildfire emergency. Strong winds drove flames deeper into the region of the Greek capital and forced fresh evacuations, France guarded a still-burning scar four times the size of Paris, while Spain's major fires stopped advancing. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the firefighters killed in the crash.

Strong winds were dying down Monday, raising hopes that the nearly 500 firefighters battling the blaze could manage to halt its advance. But authorities warned the broader Athens region of Attica remained at a high risk for wildfires due to a forecast increase in temperatures. More than 1,000 people have been evacuated from the region, including more than 250 rescued by boats from beaches in the area. Evacuation orders were issued in the early hours of Monday for three more areas, while crews worked to create firebreaks in a forest to help halt the advance of the blaze. Greece’s firefighting department said Sunday the fire apparently began from sparks emitted by a faulty power line transporting electricity from a private wind generator facility to the main electricity network.

Belgium battling biggest fire in more than a century as flames near German border and 600 people told to evacuate

Two people have died in fires on the Greek island of Salamis as firefighting aircraft were called on to help tame the biggest blaze in Belgium in more than a century in the latest wave of wildfires in Europe.

The bodies of two people were recovered from the Peristeria beach area of Salamis on Sunday after two fires broke out on the island, a fire department spokesperson told AFP. Hundreds of people have been ordered to evacuate.

In Belgium, a wildfire that broke out on Friday in the High Fens, a large nature reserve in the east of Belgium that is popular with hikers, had ravaged 3,000 hectares (7,413 acres) of land and was encroaching on the border with Germany by early Sunday morning.

About 600 people in the municipalities of Waimes and Bütgenbach, in Liège province close to the German border, were told to evacuate from their homes and tourists were advised to leave on Saturday afternoon as winds shifted and smoke spread. Of those who followed the order, about 20 spent the night in a sports hall while others sought refuge with family and friends.

Hervé Jamar, the provincial governor of Liège, said more than 250 firefighters and emergency staff were involved in the operation including firefighters from Germany.

Farmers have also been helping to battle the blaze, using their tractors to pull in water from Lake Robertville.

Air support, provided by two water-bombing aircraft from Sweden and four helicopters – two from Belgium and two from the Netherlands – is crucial owing to the nature reserve’s complex and fragile terrain, which is made up of dense forest, peat bogs and raised wooden boardwalks where heavy firefighting vehicles risk sinking.

Access to Bütgenbach lake was prohibited on Sunday in order to allow the aircraft to refill.

Authorities described the conditions as still challenging, although two fire fronts towards Jalhay and Monschau were now under control, Belgium’s interior minister, Bernard Quintin, said after visiting the crisis centre in Vottem on Sunday afternoon.

“On this third day of fighting the fires, all resources remain mobilised on the ground,” he wrote on X, and thanked all those involved. “We can also count on the solidarity of our European partners … thank you to everyone who mobilised to fight the fires. United, we are stronger.”

Five water-dropping planes and another five helicopters took off at first light Monday to help hundreds of firefighters battling a major wildfire west of Athens, Greece, a day after a midair collision between two firefighting helicopters killed two crew members.

The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe’s wildfire emergency. Flames bore down deeper into the region of the Greek capital, forcing fresh evacuations in the early hours of Monday. In France, firefighters guarded a still-burning scar four times the size of Paris.

The two crew members — one Greek and one Danish national — died when their helicopter collided with another near the seaside area of Psatha while tackling the fire that started Friday morning. The blaze raged through pine forests and scrubland through the weekend, whipped by gale-force winds that often prevented water-dropping planes from operating.

The crew of the second helicopter — a Greek and a British national — were taken to a hospital, where their injuries were reported to be light. Foreign firefighting and helicopter crews are often deployed in Greece to help tackle wildfires during the country’s hot, dry summers.

Strong winds were dying down Monday, raising hopes that the nearly 500 firefighters battling the blaze could manage to halt its advance. But authorities warned the broader Athens region of Attica remained at a high risk for wildfires due to a forecast increase in temperatures.

More than 1,000 people have been evacuated from the region, including more than 250 rescued by boats from beaches in the area. Evacuation orders were issued in the early hours of Monday for three more areas, while crews worked to create firebreaks in a forest to help halt the advance of the blaze.

Greece’s firefighting department said Sunday the fire apparently began from sparks emitted by a faulty power line transporting electricity from a private wind generator facility to the main electricity network.

Two people were arrested — an electrical engineer responsible for designing and overseeing the power project, and a contractor involved in constructing the electricity transmission network. Both face felony arson charges, while authorities had also issued an arrest warrant for the owner of the wind generator company.

payload.title: Kreikassa neljä kuollutta palojen yhteydessä, Belgiassa 600 ihmistä evakuoitiin
payload.summary: Salamiin saarelta löydettiin kaksi kuollutta, ja Ateenan länsipuolella kaksi sammutushelikopterin miehistön jäsentä kuoli ilma-alusten törmäyksessä. Belgiassa torjutaan maan suurinta metsäpaloa yli sataan vuoteen.
payload.content:
Maastopalot ovat vaatineet ihmishenkiä Kreikassa ja johtaneet laajoihin evakuointeihin sekä Kreikassa että Belgiassa. Salamiin saarella löydettiin sunnuntaina kaksi kuollutta, Ateenan länsipuolella kaksi sammutushelikopterin miehistön jäsentä kuoli ilma-alusten törmäyksessä ja Belgiassa noin 600 ihmistä määrättiin poistumaan vaara-alueelta Saksan rajan tuntumassa. Tilanteet olivat toisistaan erillisiä, mutta ne ajoittuivat samaan Euroopan maastopalojen aaltoon.

## Kreikassa kaksi erillistä kuolemaan johtanutta tapahtumaa

Kreikan palokunnan edustajan mukaan kahden ihmisen ruumiit löydettiin Salamiin saaren Peristerian ranta-alueelta sen jälkeen, kun saarella oli syttynyt sunnuntaina kaksi tulipaloa. Palokunnan edustaja kertoi löydöstä uutistoimisto AFP:lle. Salamiin tapahtuma oli erillinen Ateenan länsipuolella sattuneesta sammutushelikopterien onnettomuudesta.

Erillisessä onnettomuudessa kaksi kreikkalaista sammutushelikopteria törmäsi ilmassa torjuessaan voimakkaan tuulen ajamaa maastopaloa Ateenan länsipuolella. Toinen helikoptereista syöksyi maahan, ja kaksi miehistön jäsentä kuoli. Toinen uhreista oli Kreikan ja toinen Tanskan kansalainen. Törmäys tapahtui sunnuntaina kesken palon sammutustöiden. Pääministeri Kyriakos Mitsotakis ilmaisi surunsa onnettomuuden johdosta ja esitti osanottonsa kuolleiden palomiesten perheille.

## Attikassa yli tuhat ihmistä evakuoitu

Attikan alueen paloa torjui maanantaina lähes 500 palomiestä. Tuulen heikkeneminen lisäsi toiveita siitä, että palon eteneminen saataisiin pysäytettyä, mutta viranomaiset varoittivat palovaaran pysyvän korkeana lämpötilojen ennustetun nousun vuoksi. Alueelta oli evakuoitu yli 1 000 ihmistä, ja yli 250 heistä oli pelastettu veneillä rannoilta. Varhain maanantaina evakuointimääräyksiä annettiin vielä kolmelle alueelle. Sammutusjoukot rakensivat metsään palokatkoja liekkien etenemisen hillitsemiseksi. Varoitus korkeasta palovaarasta koski laajempaa Ateenan seutua Attikassa.

Kreikan palokunnan mukaan Attikan palo oli ilmeisesti saanut alkunsa kipinöistä, joita viallinen sähkölinja synnytti. Linjaa käytettiin sähkön siirtämiseen yksityisestä tuulivoimalasta yleiseen sähköverkkoon. Voimakkaat tuulet olivat aiemmin vieneet liekkejä syvemmälle pääkaupunkiseudulle ja pakottaneet viranomaiset määräämään uusia evakuointeja.

## Belgiassa torjutaan vuosisadan suurinta paloa

Belgiassa sammutusilma-aluksia kutsuttiin torjumaan maan suurinta metsäpaloa yli sataan vuoteen. Palo eteni lähellä Saksan rajaa, ja noin 600 ihmistä määrättiin evakuoitaviksi. Kreikan ja Belgian samanaikaiset palot kuuluivat Eurooppaa koetelleeseen maastopalojen aaltoon. Ranskassa valvottiin yhä palavaa aluetta, joka oli neljä kertaa Pariisin kokoinen, kun taas Espanjan suuret palot eivät enää edenneet.

Belgium battling biggest fire in more than a century as flames near German border and 600 people told to evacuate

Two people have died in fires on the Greek island of Salamis as firefighting aircraft were called on to help tame the biggest blaze in Belgium in more than a century in the latest wave of wildfires in Europe.

The bodies of two people were recovered from the Peristeria beach area of Salamis on Sunday after two fires broke out on the island, a fire department spokesperson told AFP. Hundreds of people have been ordered to evacuate.

In Belgium, a wildfire that broke out on Friday in the High Fens, a large nature reserve in the east of Belgium that is popular with hikers, had ravaged 3,000 hectares (7,413 acres) of land and was encroaching on the border with Germany by early Sunday morning.

About 600 people in the municipalities of Waimes and Bütgenbach, in Liège province close to the German border, were told to evacuate from their homes and tourists were advised to leave on Saturday afternoon as winds shifted and smoke spread. Of those who followed the order, about 20 spent the night in a sports hall while others sought refuge with family and friends.

Hervé Jamar, the provincial governor of Liège, said more than 250 firefighters and emergency staff were involved in the operation including firefighters from Germany.

Farmers have also been helping to battle the blaze, using their tractors to pull in water from Lake Robertville.

Air support, provided by two water-bombing aircraft from Sweden and four helicopters – two from Belgium and two from the Netherlands – is crucial owing to the nature reserve’s complex and fragile terrain, which is made up of dense forest, peat bogs and raised wooden boardwalks where heavy firefighting vehicles risk sinking.

Access to Bütgenbach lake was prohibited on Sunday in order to allow the aircraft to refill.

Authorities described the conditions as still challenging, although two fire fronts towards Jalhay and Monschau were now under control, Belgium’s interior minister, Bernard Quintin, said after visiting the crisis centre in Vottem on Sunday afternoon.

“On this third day of fighting the fires, all resources remain mobilised on the ground,” he wrote on X, and thanked all those involved. “We can also count on the solidarity of our European partners … thank you to everyone who mobilised to fight the fires. United, we are stronger.”

Five water-dropping planes and another five helicopters took off at first light Monday to help hundreds of firefighters battling a major wildfire west of Athens, Greece, a day after a midair collision between two firefighting helicopters killed two crew members.

The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe’s wildfire emergency. Flames bore down deeper into the region of the Greek capital, forcing fresh evacuations in the early hours of Monday. In France, firefighters guarded a still-burning scar four times the size of Paris.

The two crew members — one Greek and one Danish national — died when their helicopter collided with another near the seaside area of Psatha while tackling the fire that started Friday morning. The blaze raged through pine forests and scrubland through the weekend, whipped by gale-force winds that often prevented water-dropping planes from operating.

The crew of the second helicopter — a Greek and a British national — were taken to a hospital, where their injuries were reported to be light. Foreign firefighting and helicopter crews are often deployed in Greece to help tackle wildfires during the country’s hot, dry summers.

Strong winds were dying down Monday, raising hopes that the nearly 500 firefighters battling the blaze could manage to halt its advance. But authorities warned the broader Athens region of Attica remained at a high risk for wildfires due to a forecast increase in temperatures.

More than 1,000 people have been evacuated from the region, including more than 250 rescued by boats from beaches in the area. Evacuation orders were issued in the early hours of Monday for three more areas, while crews worked to create firebreaks in a forest to help halt the advance of the blaze.

Greece’s firefighting department said Sunday the fire apparently began from sparks emitted by a faulty power line transporting electricity from a private wind generator facility to the main electricity network.

Two people were arrested — an electrical engineer responsible for designing and overseeing the power project, and a contractor involved in constructing the electricity transmission network. Both face felony arson charges, while authorities had also issued an arrest warrant for the owner of the wind generator company.

article.summary: Salamiin saarelta löydettiin kaksi kuollutta, ja Ateenan länsipuolella kaksi sammutushelikopterin miehistön jäsentä kuoli ilma-alusten törmäyksessä. Belgiassa torjutaan maan suurinta metsäpaloa yli sataan vuoteen.
article.content:
Maastopalot ovat vaatineet ihmishenkiä Kreikassa ja johtaneet laajoihin evakuointeihin sekä Kreikassa että Belgiassa. Salamiin saarella löydettiin sunnuntaina kaksi kuollutta, Ateenan länsipuolella kaksi sammutushelikopterin miehistön jäsentä kuoli ilma-alusten törmäyksessä ja Belgiassa noin 600 ihmistä määrättiin poistumaan vaara-alueelta Saksan rajan tuntumassa. Tilanteet olivat toisistaan erillisiä, mutta ne ajoittuivat samaan Euroopan maastopalojen aaltoon.

## Kreikassa kaksi erillistä kuolemaan johtanutta tapahtumaa

Kreikan palokunnan edustajan mukaan kahden ihmisen ruumiit löydettiin Salamiin saaren Peristerian ranta-alueelta sen jälkeen, kun saarella oli syttynyt sunnuntaina kaksi tulipaloa. Palokunnan edustaja kertoi löydöstä uutistoimisto AFP:lle. Salamiin tapahtuma oli erillinen Ateenan länsipuolella sattuneesta sammutushelikopterien onnettomuudesta.

Erillisessä onnettomuudessa kaksi kreikkalaista sammutushelikopteria törmäsi ilmassa torjuessaan voimakkaan tuulen ajamaa maastopaloa Ateenan länsipuolella. Toinen helikoptereista syöksyi maahan, ja kaksi miehistön jäsentä kuoli. Toinen uhreista oli Kreikan ja toinen Tanskan kansalainen. Törmäys tapahtui sunnuntaina kesken palon sammutustöiden. Pääministeri Kyriakos Mitsotakis ilmaisi surunsa onnettomuuden johdosta ja esitti osanottonsa kuolleiden palomiesten perheille.

## Attikassa yli tuhat ihmistä evakuoitu

Attikan alueen paloa torjui maanantaina lähes 500 palomiestä. Tuulen heikkeneminen lisäsi toiveita siitä, että palon eteneminen saataisiin pysäytettyä, mutta viranomaiset varoittivat palovaaran pysyvän korkeana lämpötilojen ennustetun nousun vuoksi. Alueelta oli evakuoitu yli 1 000 ihmistä, ja yli 250 heistä oli pelastettu veneillä rannoilta. Varhain maanantaina evakuointimääräyksiä annettiin vielä kolmelle alueelle. Sammutusjoukot rakensivat metsään palokatkoja liekkien etenemisen hillitsemiseksi. Varoitus korkeasta palovaarasta koski laajempaa Ateenan seutua Attikassa.

Kreikan palokunnan mukaan Attikan palo oli ilmeisesti saanut alkunsa kipinöistä, joita viallinen sähkölinja synnytti. Linjaa käytettiin sähkön siirtämiseen yksityisestä tuulivoimalasta yleiseen sähköverkkoon. Voimakkaat tuulet olivat aiemmin vieneet liekkejä syvemmälle pääkaupunkiseudulle ja pakottaneet viranomaiset määräämään uusia evakuointeja.

## Belgiassa torjutaan vuosisadan suurinta paloa

Belgiassa sammutusilma-aluksia kutsuttiin torjumaan maan suurinta metsäpaloa yli sataan vuoteen. Palo eteni lähellä Saksan rajaa, ja noin 600 ihmistä määrättiin evakuoitaviksi. Kreikan ja Belgian samanaikaiset palot kuuluivat Eurooppaa koetelleeseen maastopalojen aaltoon. Ranskassa valvottiin yhä palavaa aluetta, joka oli neljä kertaa Pariisin kokoinen, kun taas Espanjan suuret palot eivät enää edenneet.
